investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: retained evidence acquired via curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion) with a descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser. A plain curl GET of the public schedule page's static HTML contained real, directly-crawlable /en/event/{slug} links (confirmed via direct text search — no JS execution needed to discover them). A plain curl GET of one such detail page returned a real schema.org Event JSON-LD block. A second detail page (a Nitsa-branded event at the same building) was independently fetched and cross-checked, confirming the same venue-level location.name.

venue_reference: Sala Apolo (concert venue/club, Poble-sec, Barcelona — including its own club-night sub-brands Nitsa and La [2] de Apolo at the same building)

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from the retained evidence at https://www.sala-apolo.com/.

site_classification.platform: A custom-built (non-WordPress) site; the public schedule page contains real, statically-crawlable event links, each leading to a page with its own schema.org Event JSON-LD block.

title.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'name' field.

start_date.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'startDate' — a non-standard 'YYYY-MM-DD (CEST|CET) HH:MM' shape (a named, universally-fixed offset abbreviation, never a seasonal guess); this package's collector reconstructs the equivalent numeric-offset ISO string mechanically before parsing.

end.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'endDate', same shape.

venue_location.notes: Each event detail page's own JSON-LD 'location.name' is the literal string 'Sala Apolo' — confirmed identical on both a plain Apolo-branded event and a Nitsa-branded event at the same building. HONEST DISCREPANCY recorded: this JSON-LD's own address states house number 113, while the venue's own /en/contact page states 107; 113 could not be independently geocoded to a specific address/POI while 107 could, so 107 is used as the canonical venue address (see venues/barcelona.json's own evidence entry for this venue).

source_record_id.notes: No numeric id is exposed; each event's own detail-page URL slug (already the source's own permanent path, discovered from the schedule page) is used as source_record_id.

event_url.notes: The event detail page's own URL.

reasons: A CONFIRMED public data path retained.
title and start_date both PROVEN (start_date via a documented, mechanical named-offset reconstruction).
source_record_id PROVEN via a documented URL-slug strategy.
recommended_family JSON_LD (already-implemented, generic family, plus a small per-venue link-discovery step).
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker. The schedule page's own bounded near-term window (documented) and the 107-vs-113 address discrepancy (documented, resolved conservatively) are MINOR, not CRITICAL.
